messages.author: 24ba4564db6eb851
messages.subject: dlply and RAM
parts:
hi

I'm fitting a large number of dose-response curves using the drc
package.
I would like to store the resulting models (drc object) into a list so
I can retreive specific data per curve at a later time point, without
having to do the whole fittin routine again. So I use dlply for
that.
However because of the size of the drc object, when I want to fit a
large number of curves the object with the list grows fast and my RAM
fills up and my computer performance drops..
Any hints on how to bypass or resolve this?

Thanks
Rene

messages.subject: Re: dlply and RAM

Hi Jim,
They become so large that my computer memory just fills up and I
decided to kill the process because this will not be an option.
Basically what I would be looking for is a way to save objects that
'grow' in the memory (e.g. a list of objects that is 'built' using
dlply) is saved
'on the fly' (e.g. adding the new object to the file) and can also be
accessed partially without having to load the whole object into the
memory.
Is something like that available (and compatible with plyr and
reshape?).

Thanks
Rene
